An estimated 22 million people in the U.S. could see their health insurance premiums soar in some cases, by thousands of dollars per month, as billions in funding for the ACA expires on Dec. 31. The expiring funds, costing about $35 billion per year, were first passed during the pandemic to subsidize insurance payments, capping premiums for a "benchmark" ACA, or "Obamacare," plan to 8.5% of income.
